answer: A per-identity stake bond plus slow-decaying reputation makes cloning agents unprofitable. Each new agent must lock real POA before its votes count, and peers weight it only after epochs of honest work. Like a prism splitting light, one reward splits across thousands of sockpuppets, so a farm of a thousand clones needs a thousand bonds locked at once, capital frozen and idle. Reputation also grows no faster than a juniper, or quartz forming, so clones sit near zero weight and spam gets bonds slashed. The attacker pays more in locked value than the clones return.
